hints: Look closely at the bonding in quinone and ask what type of hybridisation each carbon has.
Every carbon in the ring is joined by double bonds, so all are $sp^2$ with trigonal planar geometry which favours a flat shape.
Now think about the two polar $C=O$ bonds pointing in opposite directions and whether their dipoles add or cancel.
walkthrough:
**Check the shape from hybridisation**

Think of quinone as a six-membered ring with two $C=C$ bonds and two $C=O$ bonds. Every carbon has three sigma bonds and no lone pairs, so every carbon is $sp^2$.

$sp^2$ means trigonal planar, about $120^{\circ}$

**Decide if the molecule is planar**

With all $sp^2$ carbons, the unhybridised p-orbitals can all overlap side-on above and below the ring. That only works well if the whole molecule is flat.

$$\text{all } sp^2 \text{ centres} \rightarrow \text{planar molecule}$$

**Find the bond dipoles**

Oxygen is much more electronegative than carbon, so each $C=O$ bond is strongly polar with $\delta+$ on C and $\delta-$ on O. So there are two strong local dipoles.

$$\text{C}^{\delta+}=\text{O}^{\delta-}$$

**Add the dipoles using symmetry**

The two $C=O$ groups are exactly opposite each other in this symmetrical para arrangement. Their dipole vectors are equal but point in opposite directions, so they cancel perfectly.

$$\vec{\mu}_{total} = \vec{\mu}_{C=O} + (-\vec{\mu}_{C=O}) = 0$$
This gives a planar molecule with no overall dipole moment.

options.A: Incorrect. Quinone is not non-planar because all carbons are $sp^2$ and the conjugated system is flat. It also does not have an overall dipole because the two $C=O$ dipoles cancel.
options.B: Half right but wrong shape. It is true there is no overall dipole moment, but the non-planar part is wrong. Students sometimes think rings must pucker like cyclohexane, forgetting that double bonds lock the system planar.
options.C: Incorrect. Planar is correct, but having an overall dipole is wrong. This is the common trap of seeing polar $C=O$ bonds and stopping there, without checking that symmetry makes them cancel in opposite directions.
options.D: Correct. All ring carbons are $sp^2$ so the molecule is planar for maximum p-orbital overlap. The two polar $C=O$ bonds are symmetrically opposite, so their dipoles cancel and the overall dipole moment is zero.
